# dynamic-networks

A process-bigraph research workspace that turns the classic models of **network
dynamics** into a single, reusable machine. One generalized
`NetworkDynamicsProcess` reconfigures a graph through process-bigraph
`_add`/`_remove` **structural reactions**; each dynamic rule is one registered
reaction, so the whole catalog is directly comparable and extensible with a
single function per new rule. The investigation **`dynamic-networks`** has ten
studies, each showing the network evolving under one rule as an interactive
animation and a GIF.

**Family A — dynamics *of* the network** (topology reconfiguration):
Erdős–Rényi random growth · Barabási–Albert preferential attachment ·
Watts–Strogatz small-world rewiring · Bianconi–Barabási fitness ·
duplication–divergence · forest-fire densification · adaptive coevolution ·
activity-driven temporal networks.

**Family B — dynamics *on* the network** (SBML at the nodes): a real COPASI/SBML
**Repressilator** runs in every node (reusing
[viva-copasi](https://github.com/vivarium-collective/viva-copasi)) with
multi-species concentrations diffusing along the edges — operator-split
reaction–diffusion on the graph. With coupling the networked oscillators
**synchronise**; the uncoupled control stays out of phase.

The reference catalog (every rule + its primary papers) is in the workbench's
**Resources** tab (`viva_dynamic_networks/data/vg_data/structured_resources.yaml`),
and each study cites those references.

Scaffolded from
[viva-template](https://github.com/vivarium-collective/viva-template).

## Working with this workspace

The [viva-superpowers](https://github.com/vivarium-collective/viva-superpowers)
Claude Code plugin provides skills that drive the canonical PR flow:

- `/viva-study <slug>` — start a study (8-section spec, `phase: Design|Build|Simulate|Evaluate|Decide`).
- `/viva-investigation <slug>` — group related studies into an investigation (DAG via `pipeline_gate.prerequisites`).
- `/viva-expert <tool>` — wrap a simulator as a process-bigraph Process or Step (sibling repo + tests + report). Pass `--lightweight` to write in-workspace instead.
- `/viva-expert <name> <tools…>` — wire wrapped simulators into a composite (sibling repo, or `--lightweight` for in-workspace).
- `/viva-viz` — generate a Visualization from a natural-language description.
- `/viva-report` — regenerate `workspace/reports/index.html`.

Decide-phase studies can record `followup_proposals[]`; seed a child study
from any proposal with `/viva-study seed-from-followup <parent>/<proposal_id>`.

### Composites

<!-- BEGIN:composites -->
<!-- generated by `vivarium-workbench gen-readme` — edit the source, not this table -->

| Composite | What it is |
|---|---|
| `activity_driven` | Perra activity-driven temporal network: each step all edges reset, then each node fires with probability ∝ its activity and links to m random others — a blinking contact sequence. |
| `adaptive_rewire` | Gross–Blasius coevolution: opinions spread voter-style while, with rate w, nodes cut ties to differing neighbours and reconnect to like-minded ones — topology and state co-adapt. |
| `duplication_divergence` | Duplication–divergence: a new node copies a random node's edges, retaining each with probability q (optional parent link with probability p) — reproduces protein-network topology. |
| `erdos_renyi` | Random growth (Erdős–Rényi): a node arrives each step and links to each existing node with probability p. |
| `fitness_attachment` | Bianconi–Barabási: preferential attachment weighted by an intrinsic per-node fitness η — a fit latecomer can overtake older hubs. |
| `forest_fire` | Forest-fire growth: a new node burns recursively outward from a random ambassador — densification and shrinking diameter. |
| `growing_repressilator_network` | Dynamics on a GROWING topology: forest-fire growth adds Repressilator reactor-nodes over time while protein diffusion couples them — newcomers join at their own phase and entrain. (Forest-fire growth… |
| `preferential_attachment` | Barabási–Albert: a node arrives each step with m edges to existing nodes chosen with probability ∝ degree — scale-free hubs emerge ('rich get richer'). |
| `repressilator_network_coupled` | A ring of Repressilator reactors (SBML at each node, via viva-copasi) coupled by protein diffusion along the edges — the oscillators synchronise. |
| `repressilator_network_uncoupled` | The same ring of Repressilator reactors with diffusion off (D=0) — independent oscillators that stay out of phase. |
| `rewiring_repressilator_network` | Dynamics on a REWIRING topology: a ring of Repressilator reactors whose edges are continuously small-world-rewired while the coupled oscillators run. |
| `small_world_rewire` | Watts–Strogatz: on a ring lattice, rewire a random edge with probability p each step — a tidy ring dissolves into a small world (high clustering, short paths). |
<!-- END:composites -->

## Layout

Project code lives at the repo root; research state is grouped under `workspace/`
(the `.pbg/` machine state stays at the root like `.git/`). Directory locations
come from the `layout:` map in `workspace.yaml` — edit it to move things.

- `workspace.yaml` — canonical state (validated against `.pbg/schemas/workspace.schema.json`).
- `viva_dynamic_networks/` — your Python package (`core.py` exposes `build_core()`).
- `scripts/` — `lint-workspace.py`, `serve.sh`, helpers.
- `workspace/studies/`, `workspace/composites/`, `workspace/references/`, `workspace/datasets/` — research artifacts.
- `workspace/notes/` — friction logs, walkthroughs, agent transcripts, ADRs. See `workspace/notes/README.md` for the
  cleanup rule: **files under `notes/` survive cleanup sweeps by default**, because they're the
  input to the next round of infrastructure improvements.
- `.pbg/schemas/` — JSON schemas the lint + dashboard validate against.

## Cleanup conventions

Cleanup PRs (`chore(cleanup): …`, `chore(repo): trim …`) routinely remove generated files,
one-shot scripts, and stale planning docs. Two locations are off-limits to bulk cleanup:

- `workspace/notes/**` — see the rule in `workspace/notes/README.md`.
- `workspace/references/notes/**` — per-paper literature notes, used by the findings protocol.

If a specific file in either location is genuinely obsolete, delete it in its own commit
with a one-line justification per file. Don't bundle with unrelated cleanup.
